title: personal-okr-weekly-retro-lina-garcia-2026-04-22
content:
Weekly retro / check-in — Lina Garcia (Q2 2026)

Purpose: quick personal retrospective on OKR progress + blockers and next-week priorities. Mostly a scratchpad for myself and a place to collect follow-ups before I update the team tracker.

OKRs (current focus)
- Objective 1: Reduce average inference p99 latency for hosted-api by 20% (baseline: 420ms)
  - Key Result A: Implement and rollout cpu/gpu adaptive batching (target: -8% latency) — In progress, spike done, PR #9876 in review (JIRA-9876).
  - Key Result B: Ship KV-cache prewarm for popular prefixes (-6%-8% on tail) — blocked by infra quota for dedicated pools. Owning: Jordan.
  - KR status: at ~55% overall.

- Objective 2: Improve cost-per-1k-tokens on popular models by 15%
  - Key Result A: Quantization profiles for two flagship models (q4_0/q5_0 experiments) — tests show ~10% cost improvement, need regression evals.
  - Key Result B: Smart routing policy pilot for low-priority batch jobs — pilot started with 3 customers, early metrics look promising.
  - KR status: ~40% (still more evals + rollout plan).

What went well this week
- Finished spike on adaptive batching and wrote design doc with microbenchmarks. Feels like a solid path to hit O1.KR.A.
- Had good sync with SRE about quota workaround; they offered a temporary increase for the prewarm experiment (SRE ticket opened).
- Demoed routing pilot to two customers — positive feedback on latency/cost tradeoffs.

What didn't go well / blockers
- Infra quota for dedicated pools blocked KV-cache prewarm rollout. Follow-up: escalate with infra leads (Samira) and propose temporary pool.
- PR review for batching has a 3-day review lag; need to triage with reviewer to speed up (assign to reviewer and offer to pair).
- Regression evals for quantized models are taking longer than expected (test harness instability + missing reference prompts). Action: allocate 1 full day to stabilize harness.

Decisions to make
- If infra quota not available by next Tuesday, pivot: run prewarm experiment on a smaller subset of prefixes and simulate rest in-situ. Pros: keeps momentum; Cons: reduced representativeness.
- Prioritize batching PR review over other non-blocking tasks this week — call this week focus.

Next week priorities (top 3)
1) Merge adaptive batching PR and start a canary rollout to 10% of hosted traffic.
2) Stabilize regression harness and run full eval on q5_0 quantization profile.
3) Resolve infra quota or run scoped prewarm pilot.

TODOs (personal)
- [ ] File escalation doc for infra quota and schedule 1:1 with Samira (due: 2026-04-24)
- [ ] Ping reviewer on PR #9876 and schedule pairing session (due: 2026-04-23)
- [ ] Carve out day to stabilize eval harness (2026-04-25)
- [ ] Update team OKR tracker with current KR %s after canary measurements (post-rollout)

Random notes / scraps
- Consider adding a short eval set focused on long-prefix degradation — might reveal caching benefits more clearly.
- Slack convo with product-ops: timeline for Dedicated pool expansion ~mid-May; align pilots accordingly.
- Reminder: update cost model spreadsheet (drive link in team folder) after quant results.

Questions to bring to manager
- Is it OK to reallocate one headcount sprint to help stabilize test harness for 2 weeks? Impact: faster evals, small delay in a lower-priority feature.
- Approval to run a scoped customer-facing prewarm pilot without full infra quota (risk profile doc ready).

Closing thought: momentum is there on batching and routing. The main risk is external (infra quotas + PR review cycles). Focus this week is unblockers and getting the canary in traffic so we can get real measurements.

----
Version notes: informal scratchpad. Will migrate final items to the team OKR tracker and raise tickets for infra escalation.
